attributes.body_ja:
「てたまらない」は、接続助詞（せつぞくじょし）「て」と五段動詞（ごだんどうし）「堪（たま）る」（意味（いみ）：耐（た）える）の否定形（ひていけい）を組（く）み合（あ）わせた文型（ぶんけい）です。「我慢（がまん）できないほど (A) だ」や「非常（ひじょう）に (A) だ」といった意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。

この文型（ぶんけい）が、「たい」で終（お）わる動詞（どうし）と結（むす）びつくと、「どうしても (A) したい」という強（つよ）い希望（きぼう）を表（あらわ）します。一方（いっぽう）、イ形容詞（けいようし）やナ形容詞（けいようし）と結（むす）びつくと「非常（ひじょう）に (A) だ」という意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。どちらの場合（ばあい）も、耐（た）えられないほど (A) の程度（ていど）が大（おお）きいことを表（あらわ）します。

ナ形容詞（けいようし）が使（つか）われる場合（ばあい）は、いつも通（どお）り「て」の代（か）わりに「で」を使（つか）いましょう。
attributes.body:
てたまらない is made up of the conjunction particle て, and the negated form of the う-Verb 堪（たま）る meaning 'to bear', 'to endure', or 'to tolerate'. Common translations include 'to not be able to help wanting to (A)', or 'extremely (A)'.

The primary difference between both meanings is that the 'can't help but want to (A)' nuance is seen attached to verbs conjugated with たい, while the 'extremely (A)' nuance is seen conjugated with both い and な-Adjectives. In both of these situations, the more literal interpretation is 'to be unbearably (A)'.

As always, で will replace て when な-Adjectives are used.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: How to use たまらない

attributes.body: ざるを得ない expresses unavoidable action due to external circumstances, as in 行かざるを得ない (I have no choice but to go). By contrast, てたまらない conveys an intense emotional feeling that is hard to endure, as in 会いたくてたまらない (I can’t help wanting to see you). Both imply compulsion, but one is situational, the other emotional.

attributes.body: Both express intense feelings. てたまらない emphasizes degree, as in かゆくてたまらない (It’s so itchy I can’t stand it). てしょうがない also shows intensity but leans toward inevitability, as in 暇でしょうがない (I’m unbearably bored).

attributes.body: Both ことに and てたまらない express emotion, but in different ways. ことに highlights the speaker's emotional response to a situation, usually following an adjective or verb, e.g. 悲しいことに、誰も来なかった 'Sadly, no one came.' てたまらない conveys an overwhelming personal feeling, often physical or emotional, e.g. 会いたくてたまらない 'I want to see you so badly I can't stand it.'

attributes.body: Both express strong emotions. てならない often implies natural, uncontrollable feelings and sounds formal, as in 心配でならない (I can’t help but worry). てたまらない emphasizes unbearable intensity, often colloquial, as in 会いたくてたまらない (I’m dying to see you).

attributes.body: Both describe situations beyond control, but differ in meaning. てたまらない expresses unbearable feelings or desires, often casually, as in 会いたくてたまらない (I miss you so much I can’t stand it). ないわけにはいかない shows unavoidable obligation due to duty or circumstances, as in 助けないわけにはいかない (I can’t very well not help them).

attributes.body: Both convey extremes but differ in tone. Adj限りだ attaches to adjectives to show feelings at the utmost, often formal, as in 嬉しい限りだ (I’m extremely happy). てたまらない highlights intense emotions or desires that feel unbearable, used more in casual speech, as in 会いたくてたまらない (I miss you so much I can’t bear it).

attributes.body: Both express uncontrollable actions or feelings, but differ in nuance. ずにはいられない is about being compelled to act (lit. 'unable not to act'), e.g. '彼を応援せずにはいられない' ('I can't help but root for him'). てたまらない emphasizes a state or feeling that overwhelms you, e.g. '暑くてたまらない' ('It's unbearably hot') or '会いたくてたまらない' ('I want to see you so much I can't bear it').
